sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Georgia
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical hazard impacts and current exposure; scenario-based climate and poverty projections to 2030 and 2050.
sources.methodology: Country assessment combines climate, infrastructure and poverty analysis using household and hazard data.
sources.limitations: Modeled regional estimates may mask within-region variation.

sources.title: A People-Centered Approach to Inclusive Growth, Sustainability and Human Development in Georgia: Country Analysis Summary Report 2025
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in Georgia
sources.temporal_coverage: Country analysis published in 2025; summarizes current development, climate and conflict vulnerabilities and institutional status.
sources.methodology: Synthesis of official data, UN research and stakeholder workshops in May-June 2025.
sources.limitations: Intersectional framing, not a measured causal pathway.

sources.title: South Caucasus Climate Impact Profile
sources.organization: adelphi research; authored by Sam Geldin (Climatepedia)
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed regional climate and displacement context; near-term 2020-2039 and medium-term 2040-2059 scenarios.
sources.methodology: Regional synthesis of observed climate, projections and sectoral impacts across three countries.
sources.limitations: Not all cross-country findings are Georgia-specific; IDPs are localized broadly.

sources.title: Reducing the Risk of Climate-Driven Disasters in Georgia
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and Government of Georgia
sources.temporal_coverage: Ongoing programme listed for December 2018-January 2028; page reports implementation outputs and status as accessed on 2026-10-27.
sources.methodology: UNDP page reports programme implementation outputs and status.
sources.limitations: Self-reported; update date unstated, no independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Impacts of Climate Change on Georgia’s Coastal Zone: Vulnerability Assessment and Adaptation Options
sources.temporal_coverage: 2020 coastal vulnerability study; includes observed 2017 degradation estimates and projections based mainly on 2015 climate models.
sources.methodology: Reviews climate projections, coastal risks and sector impacts with expert input, consultations and cost-of-environmental-degradation analysis.
sources.limitations: Regional projections use simplified assumptions; 2017 degradation estimates are not disaggregated by municipality.

claims.paraphrase: The CCDR records over 152 deaths and US$1.2 billion in losses from hazards over decades; landslides led to dozens of villages abandoned or displaced in 40 years. Shovi’s 2023 debris flow in Racha killed at least 32 and affected over 200.
claims.limitations: Not all past losses are climate-attributed.

claims.paraphrase: Among 100-year-flood-exposed people, 12% are poor and 77% have multiple vulnerabilities; among drought-exposed people, 12.1% are poor and 80% have multiple vulnerabilities. Kakheti is most drought-exposed; 91% there face other vulnerabilities.

Under the dry/hot scenario, food-price effects raise poverty for lower-income and rural households; by 2030, rates rise up to 10.2% in Imereti, 8.0% in Mtskheta-Mtianeti, 7.8% in Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti and 7.6% in Kakheti above SPS.

The UN analysis places spatial, social, political (including unresolved conflict) and environmental (including climate) factors among intersecting sources of vulnerability. Conflict disproportionately affects forcibly displaced people, residents outside government control and communities near Abkhazia/South Ossetia ABLs.
institutions: United Nations Country Team in Georgia
claims.limitations: This framing does not say climate causes conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It says conflict and environmental factors intersect in vulnerability (PDF p.9).

claims.paraphrase: Isolated mountain communities have limited development and inadequate infrastructure; older women in small-scale agriculture are particularly climate-vulnerable.
institutions: United Nations Country Team in Georgia

claims.paraphrase: Monitoring, mapping, climate forecasting and early warnings have improved, but agricultural warnings and insurance remain weak; emergency social protection roles are unclear, with limited capacity to add beneficiaries or use municipalities as first responders.
By mid-century, heat risk covers Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti and the coast under SSP1-2.6, expanding across Kolkheti Plain under SSP3-7.0; mountainous areas face more days above 25°C under SSP3-7.0.
SSP3-7.0 projects less summer rain in the Kura-Aras Basin by mid-century, raising water-shortage and hydrological-drought risks that could prompt water-use conflict.
affected_groups: communities and water users in the Kura-Aras Basin
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The profile says shortages and drought could lead to water-use conflict (PDF p.5).

claims.paraphrase: Climate impacts compound displacement linked to episodic conflict and violence. IDPs face inadequate housing, limited services and livelihoods, plus heightened flood, drought and resource risks; much of Georgia is listed among areas with many IDPs.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It says climate impacts compound conflict-related displacement (PDF p.6).

claims.locator: Official programme page, “Results So Far,” station, agricultural climate service and landslide-monitoring entries.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports 150/154 planned weather stations in place; GECSA serves over 1,000 users in Kakheti and Shida Kartli, and landslide monitors are installed at 11 sites.
claims.limitations: User totals do not measure impact.

claims.locator: Official programme page, “Results So Far,” hazard maps, vulnerability assessment, multi-hazard information and forecasting entries.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports maps for seven hazards, vulnerability assessments and forecasting across 11 basins; the Emergency Management Service holds risk data, but public access awaits a protocol.

claims.locator: Official programme page, “Results So Far,” municipal emergency plans and community-based climate risk management entries.
claims.paraphrase: Emergency plans were adopted in six of 11 municipalities: Akhmeta, Gori, Kobuleti, Lagodekhi, Signagi and Telavi. Community plans cover 45 vulnerable western communities; measures are underway in 15 across Kintrishi, Natanebi and Supsa.

claims.locator: Official programme page, “Results So Far,” flood-protection infrastructure entry.
claims.paraphrase: Flood protection was finalized at 12 of 15 sites; the largest GCF-funded site remains under construction.

The 2020 assessment says historic wetland drainage worsens lowland flood risk and is linked to coastal erosion, particularly around Poti; dams and port works also disrupt sediment delivery, including from Khobistskali, contributing to erosion and sediment accumulation at Poti port.
claims.limitations: The study also identifies human land-use and infrastructure drivers; its 2017 cost estimates are not municipal-specific.

search_audit.outcome: No inspected source directly stated that insecurity or conflict interrupted climate-adaptation delivery; UN analysis discusses broader political risks to sustainable development, not an adaptation-specific reverse link.

search_audit.query: Georgia climate resilience capacity adaptation mountain flood early warning local government official report
search_audit.outcome: Directly opened UNDP programme results and UN country analysis on early warnings, monitoring, maps, municipal plans and remaining institutional gaps.

gaps: No inspected source directly linked active conflict or insecurity to interruption, delay or unequal delivery of climate adaptation in Georgia; broader political risks to sustainable development were not treated as an adaptation-specific reverse link.

The regional displacement source says much of Georgia has high IDP numbers but does not cross-tabulate Georgia-specific IDP locations with local climate hazards; it does not support assigning climate exposure to named conflict-affected settlements.

The UN report identifies people outside government control and communities near Abkhazia/South Ossetia ABL as conflict-affected, but the inspected sources provide limited climate-risk observations within those territories.
